texts.facts: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (Pfa Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the Pfa Act and Rules. The acc used Dhani Ram is stated to be the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s. Bikaner Sweets, from where the food article, that is, 'Laddoo' was lifted for sampling. 2. As per the complaint, on 18.10.2006, the food officials consisting of Food Inspector (FI) V.P.S. Chaudhary and Field Assistant (FA) Balwant Sah under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. K.K. Sharma reached along with their staff at the premises of M/s. Bikaner Sweets at WZ-101, Chand Nagar, Tilak Nagar, New Delhi-110018, where the accused Dhani Ram was found conducting the business of various food articles including laddoo, which were lying in an open tray meant for sale for human consumption. The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of 'Laddoo' from the said vendor, to which he agreed. The sample was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including the notice as per Form-VI, panchnama, etc. The price of sample was paid to the vendor. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 08.11.2006, the PA found the sample to be adulterated because total dye content of synthetic colour was exceeding the prescribed maximum limit of 100 ppm. Upon receipt of report, the SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by FI. After completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 09.05.2007 alleging In Re vs Sh. Dhani Ram on 5 September, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150631976/ 1 violation of section 2(ia)(a)(j) and (m) of PFA Act read with Rules 28, 29 and 30 of PFA Rules , as punishable section 7/16(1A) of PFA Act. 3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 09.05.2007. The accused appeared but never opted to file any application under section 13(2) of PFA Act thereby exercising his right to get the second counterpart of the sample to be analysed from Central Food Laboratory (CFL). 4. Based on the PA report, pre-charge evidence was recorded wherein the complainant examined PW-1 FI V. P. S. Chaudhary. On the basis of his testimony, charge was framed against the accused on 20.05.2011 for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1A) PFA Act, being violation of section 2(ia)(j) and (m) of PFA Act, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Thereafter, the witness already examined in pre-charge stage was recalled for further cross-examination in post-charge stage and additionally, PW-2 FA Balwant Sah and PW-3 Sh. K. K. Sharma (SDM/LHA) were examined in post-charge stage. 5. PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings. All these witnesses deposed about the steps undertaken by them for lifting the sample and also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, notice in Form-VI Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C, PA receipt Ex. PW-1/D and LHA receipt Ex. PW-1/E. PA report Ex. PW-1/F was received which opined the sample to be adulterated. Based on the report, investigation was carried out by PW-1 who wrote letter Ex. PW-1/G to the vendor but no reply was received. He also wrote letter Ex. PW-1/H to the STO ward no. 57 to ascertain the constitution of the business concern and it was replied that no such firm was registered. After completion of investigation, consent Ex. PW-1/I was obtained from the then Director, PFA and thereafter, complaint Ex. PW-1/J was filed in the court. Intimation letter Ex. PW-1/K along with copy of PA report were sent to the accused through post. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by the defence wherein they denied that the accused had nothing to do with the business concern or that he has been falsely implicated. 6. Statement of the accused under section 313 Cr.PC was recorded on 31.07.2014 wherein he denied the allegations. He stated that he had no relation with the business concern M/s. Bikaner Sweets and also that no intimation letter was received by him. He stated that the said shop was being run at that time by one Sh. Ravinder from whom sample was lifted a few days prior to the incident. Then on the day of incident, PFA staff was again presnet there and were threatening the said Ravinder when the accused intervened which infuriated the team. This led to false implication of the accused despite the fact that he had no relation with the shop in question. He sought to lead evidence in defence. 7. The accused examined one Sh. Naresh Baghel as DW-1. However, his cross-examination was deferred but he was never brought to witness box thereafter. As such, his statement remained incomplete and no part of such statement can be read in evidence. In Re vs Sh. Dhani Ram on 5 September, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150631976/ 2 8. Accused also examined one Sh. Attar Singh as DW-2. He deposed that the property no. WZ-101, Chand Nagar (shop in question) belonged to one Mam Chand (since expired) and the shop was being run on rent by one Ravinder who has since closed the shop and his whereabouts were not known. He claimed that accused never had any relation with Bikaner Sweet shop, though his house was opposite that shop.
texts.arguments: 9. In these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the prosecution has been able to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt against the accused as he has not been able to rebut the findings of the PA report and has also failed to establish his defence. 10. On the other hand, Ld. Legal Aid Counsel has submitted that there are various missing links in the testimony of witnesses. Ld. Counsel has strongly contended that there is no evidence to connect the accused to the shop in question. He submits that the present is a case of false implication by the PFA officials.
